hints.title: Area-Proportional Continuous Sampling
hints.text: Generating points uniformly distributed across circular disk area requires scaling radial distance according to cumulative area growth.

hints.title: Inverse Transform Sampling via Square Root
hints.text: Because disk area scales quadratically with radius, sampling radius uniformly causes clustering near center. Taking the square root of uniform random variables generates a uniform areal spread.

hints.title: Polar Coordinate Blueprint
hints.text: Generate u = random() and angle theta = 2 * pi * random(). Set radial distance r = radius * sqrt(u). Compute coordinates: x = x_center + r * cos(theta), y = y_center + r * sin(theta).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math
import random

class Solution:
    def __init__(self, radius: float, x_center: float, y_center: float):
        self.radius = radius
        self.x_center = x_center
        self.y_center = y_center

    def randPoint(self) -> list[float]:
        r = self.radius * math.sqrt(random.random())
        theta = random.random() * 2 * math.pi
        return [self.x_center + r * math.cos(theta), self.y_center + r * math.sin(theta)]
```

complexity.notes: Direct closed-form inverse transform generates valid coordinates in constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sampling radius linearly clumps samples near center with higher density.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Polar math formula avoids iterative rejection loops and guarantees deterministic execution.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct derivation using cumulative distribution function F(R) = R^2 / radius^2.
